messages:
noah-dev: heads-up: ran into a surprising behavior where Retrofit's coroutine CallAdapter doesn't propagate a higher-level deadline to OkHttp, so cancelling the suspend call leaves the HTTP call running on the platform thread. spotted on Android 14 emulator but reproducible elsewhere.

noah-dev: simplified flow: our API surface exposes suspend fun embed(...): List<Float>. callers wrap that with withTimeout(1500) to enforce latency SLO. when withTimeout cancels, we expect OkHttp to cancel the request. instead the app shows the coroutine cancelled but okhttp still shows a runningCall for ~5s and then times out separately.

tara-android: can you paste minimal repro? logs?

noah-dev: repro:
```
withTimeout(1500) {
  api.embed(request) // suspend retrofit call
}
```
logs:
```
I/Coroutine: cancelled by timeout
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/embeddings
I/OkHttp: <-- 200 (5s later)
```
we expected okhttp to get cancel() and abort earlier.

noah-dev: digging into CallAdapter implementation we use: it creates a Call and enqueues, then exposes suspend cancellable continuation. When continuation is cancelled we call call.cancel(). but on Android 14's network stack the cancellation races with a streaming request body and sometimes the native socket shutdown doesn't interrupt immediate work, leaving the dispatcher thread occupied.

vic-docs: in docs we recommend using call.timeout() to set per-call timeouts but we don't surface a helper that ties coroutine deadlines to OkHttp's per-call timeout. maybe we should add a convenience extension that sets call.timeout().timeout(duration) when the calling coroutine has a deadline.

noah-dev: suggested fix: in our CallAdapter, before enqueue, query the current coroutine context for a Job and potential timeout (using kotlinx-coroutines debug or TimeoutCancellationException?) and then apply call.timeout().timeoutMillis = remainingMillis. On cancel we still call call.cancel(), but the explicit timeout makes OkHttp fail fast even if socket shutdown is slow.

tara-android: caution: call.timeout usage interacts with OkHttp dispatcher and can throw InterruptedIOException; need tests across HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. Also need to watch API 29 where socket behavior differs. I'll add emulator matrix runs API 28-34.

ci-bot: queued job: embed-timeout-propagation (id 6247).

vic-docs: follow-up: add an example in the Kotlin SDK docs showing an extension:
```
fun Call.propagateCoroutineTimeout() {
  val ms = CoroutineTimeout.currentRemainingMillis() ?: return
  this.timeout().timeout(ms, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
}
```
and call it from adapter before enqueue. docs note: "This is best-effort; coroutine cancellation races may still allow the remote request to finish."

noah-dev: I'll prototype PR with adapter change + small unit harness that simulates streaming body stall and verifies call cancelled within 200ms of coroutine cancellation.

tara-android: add a perf note: setting per-call timeout means OkHttp will allocate timeout objects; cost should be negligible but measure it lightly in CI.

noah-dev: filing issue/PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-kotlin/issues/1203. will link flaky CI job in PR.

vic-docs: good catch. docs will include both the extension and an FAQ explaining why cancellation might not immediately close a socket on every Android release.

tara-android: thanks, will review the PR and run the emulator matrix once CI finishes.
